import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Packing

This file contains a number of open problems related to the minimal size of a square (or circle)
that can contain a given number of unit squares (or circles).
In each case, we provide a known upper bound, and ask for the least such size.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia on packing of squares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing)
- [Wikipedia on packing of circles in a circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing_in_a_circle)
- [Wikipedia on packing of circles in a square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing_in_a_square)
- Friedman, Erich (2009), "Packing unit squares in squares: a survey and new results",
  Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, 1000, Dynamic Survey 7
- Pirl, U. (1969),
  ["Der Mindestabstand von $n$ in der Einheitskreisscheibe gelegenen Punkten"](https://doi.org/10.1002/mana.19690400110),
  Mathematische Nachrichten, 40: 111–124
- A website with visualizations of packings:
  [link](https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry

open scoped NNReal

universe u

namespace SquarePacking

/--
A square of a particular side length as a subset of the Euclidean plane.
Not including border, so that squares that touch at the border are disjoint,
but a square internal to another shape is a subset of that shape.
-/
def Square (side : ℝ) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p : ℝ² | 0 < p 0 ∧ p 0 < side ∧ 0 < p 1 ∧ p 1 < side}

/--
The unit square as a subset of the Euclidean plane.
-/
def UnitSquare : Set ℝ² := Square 1

/--
A circle of a particular radius as a subset of the Euclidean plane.
The radius is a nonnegative real, so that `Circle r` is always the disc of radius $r$.
Not including border, so that circles that touch at the border are disjoint,
but a circle internal to another shape is a subset of that shape.
-/
def Circle (r : ℝ≥0) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p : ℝ² | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 < (r : ℝ) ^ 2}

/--
The unit circle as a subset of the Euclidean plane.
-/
def UnitCircle : Set ℝ² := Circle 1

/--
A structure representing a packing of `n` isometric embeddings
of a set `s` inside a (presumably larger) set `S`.
-/
structure Packing (n : ℕ) (s : Set ℝ²) (S : Set ℝ²) where
  /-- The isometric equivalences
  that represent the transformations of the base shape to their locations in the packing. -/
  embeddings : Fin n → (ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ²)
  /-- The images of the embeddings are pairwise disjoint -/
  disjoint : Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (embeddings i '' s) (embeddings j '' s)
  /-- The images of the embeddings are all inside the larger set `S` -/
  inside : ∀ i : Fin n, embeddings i '' s ⊆ S

/--
The degenerate circle is empty.
-/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem circle_zero : Circle 0 = ∅ := by
  ext p
  simp only [Circle, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_lt,
    NNReal.coe_zero, zero_pow, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true]
  positivity

/--
Eleven unit squares can be packed into a square of side length < 3.877084.

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_square)
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 51]
theorem eleven_square_packing_in_square_bound :
    Nonempty (Packing 11 UnitSquare (Square 3.877084)) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the smallest square that can contain 11 unit squares?

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_square)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_eleven_square_packing_in_square :
    IsLeast {x : ℝ | Nonempty (Packing 11 UnitSquare (Square x))} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Seventeen unit squares can be packed into a square of side length < 4.6756.

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_square)
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 51]
theorem seventeen_square_packing_in_square_bound :
    Nonempty (Packing 17 UnitSquare (Square 4.6756)) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the smallest square that can contain 17 unit squares?

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_square)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_seventeen_square_packing_in_square :
    IsLeast {x : ℝ | Nonempty (Packing 17 UnitSquare (Square x))} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Three unit squares can be packed into a circle of radius $(5 \sqrt{17}) / 16 \approx 1.288$.

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_circle)
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 51]
theorem three_square_packing_in_circle_bound :
    Nonempty (Packing 3 UnitSquare (Circle ((5 * NNReal.sqrt 17) / 16))) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the smallest circle that can contain 3 unit squares?

Reference: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_packing#In_a_circle)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_three_square_packing_in_circle :
    IsLeast {r : ℝ≥0 | Nonempty (Packing 3 UnitSquare (Circle r))} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Twenty-one unit circles can be packed into a square of side length < 9.359.

Reference: [Visualizations](https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/cirinsqu/)
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 51]
theorem twenty_one_circle_packing_in_square_bound :
    Nonempty (Packing 21 UnitCircle (Square 9.359)) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the smallest square that can contain 21 unit circles?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_twenty_one_circle_packing_in_square :
    IsLeast {x : ℝ | Nonempty (Packing 21 UnitCircle (Square x))} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
Fifteen unit circles can be packed into a circle of radius
$1 + \sqrt{6 + 2/\sqrt{5} + 4 \sqrt{1 + 2/\sqrt{5}}} \approx 4.521$.

Reference:
Graham RL, Lubachevsky BD, Nurmela KJ, Ostergard PRJ.
Dense packings of congruent circles in a circle. Discrete Math 1998;181:139–154.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 51]
theorem fifteen_circle_packing_in_circle_bound :
    Nonempty (Packing 15 UnitCircle
      (Circle (1 + NNReal.sqrt (6 + 2 / NNReal.sqrt 5 +
        4 * NNReal.sqrt (1 + 2 / NNReal.sqrt 5))))) := by
  sorry

/--
What is the smallest circle that can contain 15 unit circles?

Reference:
Graham RL, Lubachevsky BD, Nurmela KJ, Ostergard PRJ.
Dense packings of congruent circles in a circle. Discrete Math 1998;181:139–154.
[Pirl (1969)](https://doi.org/10.1002/mana.19690400110) conjectured this configuration to be optimal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem least_fifteen_circle_packing_in_circle :
    IsLeast {r : ℝ≥0 | Nonempty (Packing 15 UnitCircle (Circle r))} answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end SquarePacking

findings.description: The docstring says that a square of side length strictly less than 3.877084 suffices, but the Lean proposition exhibits a packing only in `Square 3.877084`. This records a valid non-strict upper bound, not the strict bound described. Using open interiors does not supply a strict margin: boundary contacts remain permitted.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, Square packing, “In a square,” describes Trump's packing near 3.877084. The maintained packing catalogue gives its side as 3.87708359002281…, strictly below the displayed bound: https://kingbird.myphotos.cc/packing/squares_in_squares.html, entry 11.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “of side length 3.877084,” or retain the strict wording and state `∃ x : ℝ, x < 3.877084 ∧ Nonempty (Packing 11 UnitSquare (Square x))`.

findings.description: The docstring states a strict upper bound `< 4.6756`, whereas `Nonempty (Packing 17 UnitSquare (Square 4.6756))` only certifies feasibility at 4.6756. The numerical upper bound is valid; the discrepancy is limited to the strict wording in the documentation.
findings.source_evidence: Friedman's cited survey explicitly labels Figure 12 `s(17) < 4.6756`: https://www.combinatorics.org/files/Surveys/ds7/ds7v5-2009/ds7-2009.html. The maintained catalogue gives 4.67553009360455… for Bidwell's packing.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “of side length 4.6756,” or strengthen the statement to `∃ x : ℝ, x < 4.6756 ∧ Nonempty (Packing 17 UnitSquare (Square x))`.

findings.description: The docstring claims feasibility at a side length strictly below 9.359, but the proposition only asserts a packing in `Square 9.359`. This is a correct non-strict upper bound, so it does not compromise the minimum-size problem.
findings.source_evidence: The cited Friedman page gives `s = 9.358+` for 21 unit circles: https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/cirinsqu/. Its linked Packomania table gives the unit-radius side-length ratio 9.3580199589, below 9.359: https://www.packomania.com/csq/csq.html, row 21.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “of side length 9.359,” or state `∃ x : ℝ, x < 9.359 ∧ Nonempty (Packing 21 UnitCircle (Square x))` to express the strict bound.

status_issues.source_status: Solved by Kari J. Nurmela and Patric R. J. Östergård in 1999. They proved the optimal packings through n=27, including n=21. The optimal enclosing side for unit-radius circles is approximately 9.3580199589.
status_issues.evidence: The directly cited Friedman page says for n=21: “Proved by Nurmela and Östergård in 1999” (https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/cirinsqu/). The primary paper, More Optimal Packings of Equal Circles in a Square, gives d21 ≈ 0.2718122553 in Table 2 and explicitly discusses the successful n=21 optimality proof on p. 450 (https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/PL00009472.pdf). Its normalization gives L = 2 + 2/d21.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and cite the 1999 proof. The answer can be represented by the proven configuration's exact size, using its certified defining equations if necessary; 9.359 is only a loose upper bound, not the exact answer.

reformulations.difference: The file uses open square/disc interiors, disjoint images, and containment in an open container, rather than closed bodies contained in a closed container with pairwise disjoint interiors.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a unit closed square or disc C, closure(interior C) = C. An isometry equivalence is a homeomorphism, so it commutes with interiors and closures. For every closed container K, the open set e''interior C is contained in interior K iff it is contained in K, which holds iff e''C is contained in K. Disjointness of the open images is precisely disjointness of the closed images' interiors. The scratch file proves all four square/disc packing equivalences for every n, every real square side, and every nonnegative circle radius, including degenerate containers. Thus boundary touching and attainment of the minimum are preserved.

reformulations.difference: Graham et al. initially fix the enclosing circle's radius to 1 and maximize the packed circles' common radius; Lean fixes the packed circles' radius to 1 and minimizes the enclosing radius.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Scaling a packing with inner radius r > 0 and outer radius 1 by 1/r gives unit-radius pieces in an enclosing circle of radius R = 1/r, and the inverse scaling reverses this construction. Reciprocation reverses the optimization order. The paper explicitly gives this equivalent radius-ratio formulation on p. 140, together with R = 1 + 2/d for its point-separation normalization. Wikipedia uses the same unit-inner-radius convention as Lean.

sources_consulted: Friedman, Packing Unit Squares in Squares: A Survey and New Results (2009), introduction, Figures 6 and 12, and appendix: https://www.combinatorics.org/files/Surveys/ds7/ds7v5-2009/ds7-2009.html

Graham, Lubachevsky, Nurmela and Östergård, Dense packings of congruent circles in a circle, Discrete Mathematics 181 (1998), especially pp. 139–142 and Table 1 on p. 152: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/98_01_circles.pdf

Nurmela and Östergård, More Optimal Packings of Equal Circles in a Square, Discrete & Computational Geometry 22 (1999), especially introduction, Table 2, and the n=21 discussion on p. 450: https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/PL00009472.pdf

review.notes: All 16 declarations were reviewed. No substantive mathematical misformalization was found; the three findings are documentation-only strict/non-strict discrepancies. The other four research-open tags agree with the consulted sources. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings and contains boundary tests, non-vacuity checks, and four independent open/closed packing equivalence proofs; these proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The five IsLeast answer slots have the intended real/nonnegative-real types and constrain their answers to actual minima. Pirl's original 1969 article could not be accessed directly (Wiley returned HTTP 403); the fifteen-circle statements and attribution were checked against the other cited sources, including Wikipedia and Graham et al. The target file remains identical to its committed content.
